focus: Angle 14 — roster completeness for the seventh executor

findingDetails.title: cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md omits cli-hermes from all three prose roster statements while its own machine block and the compiled router carry the mode
findingDetails.evidence: cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md states a six-mode roster in all three prose statements (:24-25 hub-selects list, :46-64 per-mode leaf bullets with no cli-hermes bullet, :145-146 defer instruction to confirm the target executor) while the same file machine block names HERMES in INTENT_SIGNALS (:96) and RESOURCE_MAP (:124-126), mode-registry.json registers cli-hermes (:212-236), and compiled-route.cjs executed this iteration resolves hermes prompts to workflowMode cli-hermes.
findingDetails.impact: An agent following the hub's front-door doc sees six modes, has no leaf mapping for cli-hermes, and is told to confirm one of six executors; the machine block in the same file names seven, so the document disagrees with itself at the layer that governs manual routing. Wave-one F007 filed the same three statements at P0 and left one downgrade path (ROUTER.md shown superseded and marked non-authoritative); inspected this iteration, no supersession exists and SKILL.md:74 still names ROUTER.md the stage-two authority, so this lane adopts P0 on re-adjudication.
findingDetails.recommendation: Name cli-hermes in all three statements and add its leaf bullet, or replace the hand-written rosters with a pointer to mode-registry.json. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read ROUTER.md end to end (three roster sites confirmed, no seventh bullet), verified the HERMES intent and resource entries in the same file, confirmed the registry entry and executed the compiled route front door with hermes prompts. Re-read SKILL.md:74 and hub-router.json to test wave one's supersession downgrade path; both confirm ROUTER.md remains the designated stage-two authority.

findingDetails.title: Hub SKILL.md files carry hand-written mode counts their own registries contradict
findingDetails.evidence: cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:74 says the surface router defines the leaf-intent model for all six modes against :54 same file All seven modes are primary and 7 registered modes; system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:80 says the 3 improvement modes share the deep-improvement packet against 2 registered (agent-improvement, model-benchmark); system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:131 says six registered modes against 5 registered and description.json:3 five modes.
findingDetails.impact: Three count statements across two hub front doors misstate the mode set their own registries define; nothing reads prose counts, so the drift persists across releases.
findingDetails.recommendation: State counts from mode-registry.json, or drop the numeral and reference the registry. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Parsed all three mode-registry.json files to count registered modes (5/6/7), read each numeric count statement at its line, and checked the sibling description.json statement in system-deep-loop for the correct count.

findingDetails.title: Deep-loop protocol and packet prose under-describes the executor set, and the council packet's prose contradicts its own resolver
findingDetails.evidence: deep-review/references/protocol/loop-protocol.md:281 closes the executor-resolution section with the seven-kind authority is executor-config.ts after naming cli-codex, cli-cursor, cli-devin, cli-pi and omitting cli-hermes (which executor-config.ts:11 declares and fanout-run.cjs:2721 implements; hermes appears nowhere in the review protocol); deep-research/SKILL.md:267 repeats the same seven-kind framing without hermes; deep-ai-council/SKILL.md:22 states the resolver accepts native/cli-opencode/cli-cursor/cli-devin/cli-pi/opencode while orchestrate-session.cjs:198 accepts cli-hermes and the same SKILL.md lists hermes rounds at :26 and :357; both council YAMLs repeat the short list at :26.
findingDetails.impact: A reader of any of these sentences under-provisions a supported capability; the council sentence reads the opposite of what the code does.
findingDetails.recommendation: Name cli-hermes in each enumeration (or reference EXECUTOR_KINDS), and correct the seven-kind count to the authority's eight. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read both loop protocols, the research SKILL section, the council SKILL sections and both council YAMLs at their lines, then traced the council accept list to the resolver code that permits cli-hermes.

findingDetails.title: Deep-loop catalogs describe the executor dispatcher as three kinds (twice with a duplicated kind name) against a driver that implements eight
findingDetails.evidence: deep-review/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md:150 and loop-lifecycle/executor-selection-contract.md:3,:29-35 describe parseExecutorConfig as one of three dispatch branches (native, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code) against the 8-kind schema; runtime/feature-catalog/fanout/fanout-run.md:42 says Supports all 3 CLI kinds: cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, cli-opencode against fanout-run.cjs:2717-2722 eight adapters; deep-improvement model-dispatcher.md:27 says across cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, and cli-opencode against dispatch-model.cjs:138-145 six KNOWN_EXECUTORS; scripts/model-benchmark/README.md:75 says routes to cli-opencode or cli-claude-code.
findingDetails.impact: Four catalog sites understate what the dispatcher supports by 3-6 kinds, and the duplicated cli-opencode in two of them marks a botched rename that makes the wrong claim harder to notice.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct the counts and kind names in the four sites from the source files; check for further duplicated-name substitutions in the same documents. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read each catalog claim at its line and compared it to the subject source: fanout-run.cjs adapter map (8) and dispatch-model.cjs KNOWN_EXECUTORS (6), both read directly.

findingDetails.title: cli-* packet sibling lists froze at each packet's authoring date, leaving the newest siblings out of six files
findingDetails.evidence: cli-claude-code/SKILL.md:381 lists cli-opencode twice and no cli-pi or cli-hermes; cli-codex/SKILL.md:383 names 2 siblings, cli-cursor/SKILL.md:416 three, cli-devin/SKILL.md:464 four, cli-pi/SKILL.md:303 five, while cli-hermes/SKILL.md:345 names all six; cli-devin/references/integration-patterns.md:30 still says Devin is the 5th executor kind in the cli-* family (5th of seven) and cli-pi/references/pi-tools.md:17 enumerates five sibling packets without cli-hermes; the four older packet READMEs do carry a cli-hermes row.
findingDetails.impact: Each older packet's prose roster omits at least the newest two siblings; the duplicate cli-opencode in cli-claude-code displaces cli-codex, so a reader cannot recover the intended list from the file.
findingDetails.recommendation: Update each sibling list (or replace it with a pointer to mode-registry.json), and fix the duplicated-name slots from the packet's intended provider. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the Related-skills closure of all seven cli-* SKILL.md files plus both named reference files, and checked the packet README rows to confirm the READMEs were updated while the SKILL.md lists were not.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: A fleet-wide statement census across three hubs, four artifact classes, two compiled contracts and six command YAMLs, with the authority/consumer split verified by reading the executor schema, the fan-out adapter map, and executing the compiled front door.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 14 asks for every roster statement across the hubs, catalogs, playbooks and protocols; the authority side (executor schema, fan-out adapter map, compiled contracts, registries) was read first so every prose statement could be judged against a machine control.

searchLedger.invariant: A hub's prose routing statements name every mode its registry registers.

searchActions.queryOrPath: ROUTER.md overview (:1-40), per-mode leaf bullets (:40-70), machine block (:85-130), how-to-read (:130-150)
searchActions.result: Three prose roster statements each listing six modes; no cli-hermes leaf bullet; the same file's machine block carries HERMES intent signals and resource entries.

searchLedger.rationale: All three hypothesis arms the angle names are confirmed; the file contradicts its own machine block in three places.

searchLedger.invariant: A numeric mode count in a front-door doc equals the registry count.

searchActions.queryOrPath: mode counts from the three mode-registry.json files, compared against each numeric count statement in the hub SKILL.md files
searchActions.result: Registry counts 5/6/7; cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:74 states six against seven; system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:80 states 3 improvement modes against two; :131 states six registered against five.

searchLedger.rationale: Three count statements drift from the registry authority with no reader or gate to catch them.

searchLedger.invariant: Every executor-kind enumeration names all kinds the authority declares, or references the authority.

searchActions.queryOrPath: review and research executor-resolution prose, council resolver paragraph, both council YAML seat parameter lines
searchActions.result: Review protocol and research SKILL state seven kinds and omit cli-hermes; the council SKILL accept list omits cli-hermes while the resolver code accepts it.
Line 198 accepts native, cli-opencode, cli-cursor, cli-devin, cli-pi, cli-hermes and the opencode alias — contradicting the SKILL.md sentence.

searchLedger.rationale: The prose undercounts in two protocols and, in the council packet, states the opposite of the resolver.

searchLedger.invariant: A catalog's capability claim matches the source file it describes.

searchActions.queryOrPath: catalog executor-kind claims vs fanout-run.cjs LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS and dispatch-model.cjs KNOWN_EXECUTORS
searchActions.result: Catalog claims: one of three branches, all 3 CLI kinds (with cli-opencode duplicated), across cli-opencode/cli-claude-code/cli-opencode, routes to cli-opencode or cli-claude-code. Sources: 8 adapters, 6 dispatcher kinds.

searchLedger.rationale: Four catalog sites understate their subject, two with a duplicated kind name consistent with a botched substitution.

searchLedger.invariant: A packet's sibling list names every current sibling.

searchActions.queryOrPath: Related-skills closure of all seven cli-* packets plus the two reference files that enumerate siblings
searchActions.result: Lists contain 1-5 unique siblings with the count increasing by authoring date; cli-claude-code duplicates cli-opencode; only cli-hermes names all six; READMEs carry hermes rows the SKILL.md lists lack.

searchLedger.rationale: The freeze pattern is monotonic and complete across the packet family; the newest packet is the only complete list.

searchLedger.hypothesis: cli-hermes routing could be broken at the compiled layer, making the prose omission moot.

searchActions.queryOrPath: compiled-route.cjs --hub cli-external-orchestration with two hermes prompts
searchActions.result: Both resolve workflowMode cli-hermes (generation 5, policy hash 06b19646b9f49698269036fff4f3d78fb3a7e524f7620975069c0235f91923b4); capability is intact and the defect is statement coverage only.

searchLedger.rationale: Routing works; the angle's framing that the question is statements, not capability, is confirmed.

searchLedger.hypothesis: if_cli_copilot branches prove a roster kind was removed without cleaning the workflow assets.

searchActions.queryOrPath: EXECUTOR_KINDS against the three if_cli_copilot branches and the review-auto branch comment
searchActions.result: cli-copilot is absent from the schema; the branch comment (:1121-1123) states there is no cli-copilot kind and dispatches it as kind:'native'; read as deliberate legacy retention, not a live enum violation.

searchLedger.rationale: Recorded as an observation and handed to the angle-16 variant census; not filed as a roster finding.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Single-executor cli-hermes has no branch key of its own and could fall through the executor dispatch step.

searchActions.queryOrPath: grep .opencode/bin and .opencode/skills for readers of branch_on / if_cli_* keys
searchActions.result: No in-repo consumer of the branch keys exists; the branch matcher lives outside the repository, so whether the cli-pi branch (whose notes assert cli-hermes support at review-auto:1829) receives cli-hermes or the kind falls through cannot be proven from the tree.

searchLedger.rationale: Blocked on an external component; carried as unresolved rather than filed, with the exact resolution path (read the runner's branch matcher or run a single-executor cli-hermes review) recorded in the iteration file.
